text: Few debates are as heated as the one about job displacement. Across the labour market, a widening skills gap leaves employers short of talent, while thousands face redundancy. steps.title: Đọc mới
steps.heading: Automation: a balanced view
steps.purpose: Đọc để tìm: tác giả đề xuất giải pháp nào?
text: The debate about automation is often reduced to slogans. In truth, job displacement is only one part of a wider story. In the labour market, a persistent skills gap coexists with redundancy, and the workforce is increasingly shaped by the gig economy; those who fail to adapt may be made redundant. On the positive side, firms claim that new tools boost productivity, cut costs and streamline operations. Cutting-edge, labour-saving technology lets them reap the benefits, yet it remains a double-edged sword. Critics counter that it will widen the inequality gap, weaken job security and create a growing sense of insecurity. Overreliance on algorithms can erode skills, and systems that put people out of work may fall short of what society expects. The answer is neither panic nor complacency. Governments should help people reskill, support lifelong learning, and adapt to change. They must strike a balance between growth and fairness, build a safety net, and treat this as a pressing issue so as to mitigate the impact. Seldom has the choice mattered so much.
